scope_note: Rounds 1-3 validated the conv-as-streaming fixed-kernel formulation in 2D (Taylor-Green decay + plane Poiseuille) and, in 3D, only the *operator* (conv3d vs canonical roll traversal on a random field). Round 4 asks the question rounds 1-3 never asked: does the same fixed-kernel transport plus 1x1 bounce convolution reproduce physics in 3D against closed-form 3D solutions, with a solid mask that is not a single flat wall?
decision: Keep the D3Q19 fixed-kernel transport + bounce_blend as a drop-in 3D transport option for TensorLBM (same adoption decision as rounds 1-3, now with 3D physical evidence), or restrict the option to 2D if 3D fails a predeclared KPI.

alternatives.A_native_gather_3d: gather over shifted source cells with modulo indexing on a (19, nz, ny, nx) field -- the 3D analogue of tensorlbm.solver.stream (which is 2D-only); wall bounce as explicit direction reversal at solid nodes.
alternatives.B_conv_fixed_kernel_3d: tensorlbm.streaming_conv.stream_conv_3d -- one fixed 3x3x3 depthwise cross-correlation (tap index 1 - c_axis) over circular-padded fields; wall bounce via streaming_conv.bounce_blend (1x1 cross-channel convolution through the solid mask).
alternatives.REF_analytic_3d: closed-form references only: (i) 3D Stokes-mode decay of a divergence-free Fourier mode with |k|^2 = kx^2+ky^2+kz^2, velocity decay exponent nu*|k|^2 exact; (ii) plane Poiseuille parabola for a 3D slit channel (walls in y only, periodic x and z); (iii) Boussinesq series solution of the square duct, self-checked here by finite-difference Poisson residual and by its friction-velocity product f*Re = 56.908 (Shah & London 1978).

hypothesis: H1: in 3D, replacing only the transport operator (A -> B) leaves the population field bit-wise identical, the Stokes decay exponent within 3% of nu*|k|^2, the 3D slit-channel profile within 3% of the parabola, and the square-duct centreline velocity and f*Re within 3% of the series/literature values (owner gate 15%). H0 (falsifier): any predeclared KPI at or beyond the 15% owner gate, or the two arms not bit-identical.

metrics.arm_pair_max_rel: max|u_A - u_B| / max|u_A| over all fluid nodes at the final step (dimensionless)
metrics.f_sha256_equal: sha256 of the final population field is equal between arms (bit-wise equivalence under walls + forcing)
metrics.gamma_fit_rel_err_pct: fitted velocity decay exponent vs nu*|k|^2 for the 3D Stokes mode (percent)
metrics.gamma_fit_r2: coefficient of determination of the ln(max|u|) least-squares fit
metrics.profile_l2_pct_slit: ||u_num(y) - u_parabola(y)||_2 / ||u_parabola||_2 over fluid rows of the 3D slit channel (percent)
metrics.peak_rel_err_pct_slit: |u_max_num - u_max_analytic| / u_max_analytic for the slit channel (percent)
metrics.fRe_rel_err_pct_duct: f*Re from the numerical mean velocity vs 56.908 (percent)
metrics.step_cost_ratio: wall time per step, conv arm / gather arm (dimensionless; informational, not a gate)

unit_of_analysis: one transport arm at one 3D configuration; every KPI is a scalar per arm-configuration

baseline_control.baseline: arm A at the coarsest configuration of each case
baseline_control.control: arm B at the identical configuration: the single changed variable is the transport/bounce operator; collision (BGK), forcing source, initial condition, sampling schedule, dtype and thread count are shared code
baseline_control.reference: closed forms and a literature constant, never another LBM implementation

predeclared_thresholds.note: the duct series is itself a judge, so it is validated before use: FD Poisson residual and f*Re against 56.908 must be inside 1%, otherwise the duct KPI is reported as WITHHELD rather than pass/fail

sensitivity_points: 3D Stokes mode: n in {24, 32} at k = 2*pi/n in each axis, A = 1e-3 (Stokes regime), tau = 0.8
3D slit channel: Ny in {12, 16, 24} at tau = 0.8, u_max_target = 0.02
square duct: n in {12, 16} at tau = 0.8, u_max_target = 0.02
stopping_rule: fixed step counts predeclared from the analytic time scales before any run: Stokes mode 800 steps (about 7 e-folding times at nu = 0.1, n = 32); slit channel and square duct 30000 steps (the same viscous-time budget rounds 2-3 used for the 2D channel, H^2/nu scaled by the duct side). No arm is extended or truncated after inspecting a KPI.
variables_changed: bounce operator (index reversal vs 1x1 conv blend)
confounders: half-way wall placement: analytical references are evaluated at the half-way wall planes (wall at 0.5 and N-1.5), so no O(1) offset is embedded in the comparison
duct corners: the series has a corner singularity, so the cross-section L2 KPI is expected to converge slower than the 2D profile KPI; the centreline and f*Re KPIs are the corner-free ones
compressibility: the Stokes-mode amplitude is set to 1e-3 so that O(Ma^2) terms are below 1e-6 relative
repetition_rationale: each configuration is deterministic (fixed initial condition, no RNG except in the random-field equivalence probe, which is seeded); a repeat must reproduce bit-wise, so a single deterministic run per configuration is sufficient and the reproducibility claim is checked by re-running one configuration
environment: CPU torch float64, torch.set_num_threads(4), commit + dirty flag recorded in result.json
analysis_plan: per case: (1) arm-pair bit-wise comparison; (2) each arm against its closed-form reference; (3) failure modes reported as-is (non-finite populations, |u| > 10*u_target, non-converged steady state via half-run drift)
